doc.title: Bill Charlap interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, Arizona, April 16, 2000

title: His father Moose Charlap, Peter Pan songs, and a house full of songwriters
summary: His father wrote most of the Peter Pan music and died when Bill was six or seven; songwriters visited the house, and his own daughters now meet musicians unawares.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: like “I’m Flying,” “I’ve Gotta Crow,” “Tender Shepherd,” “I Won’t Grow Up,” that’s all my dad, as many pop songs such as “I Was Telling Her About You,” you might know that one, Joe Williams did that, Betty Carter used to sing it I hear. And many others. He died when I was quite young, I was six or seven years old. And he was only in his 40s, so he would have gone on. But my parents are both related very closely, they lived in the tradition of the American popular song, and that is a very focal point for me, it’s a center point for what my being is about as a musician.
So you were surrounded by that in your house as you grew up, that music.

Yes. Certainly that energy. My father was composing, sitting at the piano composing, and there were many well known songwriters and lyricists who would come by our place. So I took that all pretty much for granted. They were just — kids don’t know any of that sort of stuff. And I think now my daughters, I have Sophie and Vivian, Vivian’s only seven months old at the time of this taping, Sophie is almost three years old. And they’ve met many very important jazz musicians through their life, but they don’t know it, it’s just Uncle Keter, you know.
